rubrics.justification: The response overstates embryo quality from the image, describing a compact ICM and reasonably continuous/good-cell-number TE, whereas the image and provided grade 2AB suggest a less expanded blastocyst with loose/sparse TE. It also introduces stage 3-4 ambiguity despite the stated Gardner 2.

It integrates age, diagnosis, prior live births, BMI, ovarian reserve, semen, and lifestyle reasonably well with prognosis, though some points are generic and the AMH/MII discussion is only loosely tied to this transfer.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a plausible link from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis. Minor issues arise from overstating morphology and calling the embryo 'strong-quality' despite a 2AB grade.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET, attention to hydrosalpinx, review of uterine factors, and avoiding unsupported add-ons. Slight overinterpretation of morphology and somewhat optimistic framing prevent a top score.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx assessment, endometrial review, and when to escalate evaluation. Useful but not highly tailored beyond standard IVF management.
